Some hockey purists would love for the NHL to get rid of the shoot-out. Those of us with this bent dislike how games are decided in this manner.

As Commissioner, I would tweak the points awarded to victors and losers based on what period the game is won. Teams would be given more points to win games in regulation, with the incentive dwindling as the games get decided in OT or SO. 

For example, the winning team would be awarded 3 points for games won in regulation, 2 points in OT, and 1 point in SO. The losing team would be awarded 1 point in regulation, 0.5 points in OT, and 0 points in SO. 

There are several advantages to proposing this points system:

1. Fewer games would be decided by SO.

2. Games could be decided earlier as teams would strive to win in regulation. 

3. Teams that can win more consistently in regulation would realize a greater points differential throughout the season.

4. Losing teams would be awarded fewer points.

5. More stats for us junkies!

When authors were on more than one guideline, it was also common that they disclosed different FCOI in each. Guidelines generally identified affiliations with organizations and approximately half of those organizations disclosed FCOI relationships with drug companies.

The grace of the Mass is not of human doing. My wife and I have received grace upon grace after we started attending the TLM. We first referred to it as the Shekinah Glory, after the Light that shone forth from the Mercy Seat once a year, on the Day of Atonement, and which only the High Priest saw, in ancient Jerusalem. Then we found out that this Eucharistic vision is known to the tradition, and is called the Uncreated Light, and also the Tabor Light (Mt. Tabor is the mount of the Transfiguration).
